title: Converge control primitives (buttons/tables/charts) into single responsive primitives set and sanitize layer names
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We will consolidate small, medium, and large button variants plus the related primitive table and chart control components into a single "primitive controls" set that adapts via explicit semantic tokens and responsive auto-layout rules. The goal is to reduce duplication, fix inconsistent layer names, and make publishing predictable without breaking downstream pages that reference older instances.

Why now:
- Multiple teams are creating near-duplicate components (size/spacing drift).
- Layer names are inconsistent across files which breaks some automated extractors and token sync flows.
- Publishing currently causes unexpected instance mismatches; we want a phased publish that preserves instance mapping.

Scope & goals:
- Create a single primitives page (Buttons, Inputs, Selects, Table row controls, Small chart legend items) with canonical semantic token bindings for size, spacing, and color (e.g., token.button.height-sm, token.spacing.xs).
- Standardize layer naming convention: <role> / <element> / <state> (e.g., btn / label / hover). Run rename script and validate.
- Replace fragile frame constraints with responsive auto-layout rules and explicit resize constraints so instances resize predictably in product files.
- Publish in two waves: (1) internal docs + playgrounds (canary), (2) wide publish to libraries with migration notes and rollback plan.
- Add QA checklist and deprecation mapping for old components.

Acceptance criteria:
- All primitives exist on a single Figma page named "Primitives - Controls" with clear token bindings documented in the file.
- Layer names conform to the new naming standard with 95% automated coverage from rename pass; remaining manual fixes documented.
- No visual diffs > 2px for high-use instances in the canary playground (measured via visual snapshot tool).
- Publish Wave 1 completed and verified; migration doc and rollback plan posted to Confluence.
- Designer + PM + two engineers have signed off in comments and the PR is linked.

Work breakdown (high level):
1) Audit existing components (buttons / table controls / chart legends) and inventory instances across 12 product files. (Maya / 3 days)
2) Draft canonical primitives and token map, get PM sign-off. (Jonah / 2 days)
3) Implement responsive auto-layout constraints and swap in tokens. Run "Rename It" plugin and a small script to normalize names. (Jonah / 2 days)
4) Create canary playground and run snapshot diffs; iterate until within thresholds. (QA + Eng / 2 days)
5) Publish Wave 1, monitor issues for 48 hours, then Wave 2. (Design Ops / 1 day + monitoring)

Trade-offs & decisions made so far:
- Chose to prefer semantic token bindings over inline numeric values to make future token swaps low-risk. This required a short mapping step for legacy instances.
- Decided NOT to collapse chart legend glyphs into a single compound component in this ticket; doing so increases risk and will be tracked as follow-up.
- Will keep deprecated components in an archive page with a migration table so product teams can migrate on their timetable instead of forcing a bulk change.

Migration & rollback plan:
- Before wide publish, create a migration sheet (Confluence) that maps old component keys to new ones, with screenshots and example instance updates.
- If Wave 1 exposes > 5 regressions in product pages, rollback and add manual instance-updates as patch PRs.

Links to artifacts:
- Figma working file (canary): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/primitives-controls-canary
- Confluence migration doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Primitives+Consolidation+Plan
- GH PR (rename script + docs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/482
- Visual snapshot report: https://internal.redwood.ai/visual-reports/PR-482

Next steps (today):
- Run instance inventory export and share per-product CSV with eng leads (assigned: Jonah).
- Schedule 30m sign-off meeting with PM (Aisha) and two engineers for Thurs 2025-02-20.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to auto-layout behavior inside tables — there are known constraints issues with nested grids; I left two examples marked "manual-fix" for discussion.
- Accessibility: token color contrasts were validated for primary/disabled states; please flag any contextual contrast problems in comments.
